facts.note: The whole site, shore to lantern, across the region's long axis.
The width of the headland the site stands on.
The plane the sea reaches: the shingle and the drowned pans.
The works terrace, one storey clear of the highest tide.
The abbey precinct, one storey above the works it owned.
The headland, where the ground stops rising.
The boiling house is a square of thirty-two: four pans, four furnaces, eight blocks a bay.
Its clerestory sits fourteen above the floor. The same storey the church gets, because the same masons cut both.
The nave takes the boiling house's storey exactly. This is the identity the whole silhouette rests on.
The walled court at the foot of the light: one bay of the boiling house, squared.
How far the light is from the beach the party lands on — far enough that it reads as a destination from the first frame.
